title: Gluing dimension-normalized Hilbert--Samuel and marked-ideal words
statement:
Over $\mathbf Q$, consider all closed embeddings $X\hookrightarrow P$ with $X$ reduced and $P$ smooth, separated and of finite type, including empty schemes and finite disjoint unions [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix the simultaneous marked-ideal numerical word assignment of [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine]. For a point $x$ of a strict transform, put $h_x(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X_H,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{n+1})$, let $q_x$ be the minimum dimension of its local irreducible components and $c_x$ the number of distinct such dimensions, and set $A_x=(c_x,\Delta^{q_x}h_x)$, where $\Delta f(0)=f(0)$ and $\Delta f(n+1)=f(n+1)-f(n)$ [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-smooth-dimension-profile]. At a singular point take a maximal-order codimension-zero presentation in a minimal smooth envelope [lem-trf-hilbert-samuel-local-presentations]. Delete the leading entry $1$ of its marked-ideal word, retaining its remaining tail $t_x$, the ordered earlier center ideals, and the birth stages of the exceptional components. For each chosen presentation, distinguish its recorded earlier history from its test boundary: the latter starts empty when the presentation is chosen and records only divisors subsequently created by its test operations. Set $w_H(x)=(A_x,t_x)$ at singular points, and $w_H(x)=\bot$ at regular points.

These prescriptions define one simultaneous assignment in a fixed totally ordered lexicographic word space with a new least element $\bot$, on finite admissible histories relative to this assignment [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history], without assuming those histories terminate. In particular, the local prescriptions agree on overlaps and under equivalent minimal-envelope presentations. At transformed stages the controlled transforms of the presenting marked ideals give this same word on the scheme-theoretic strict transforms. For every finite-type stage $X_H$, the function $w_H$ has finite image, and each upper level set $\{x:w_H(x)\geq v\}$ is closed. It equals $\bot$ exactly at regular points. For every fixed $D\geq\dim X_H$, replacing the second entry of every head by $\Lambda^D\Delta^{q_x}h_x$, where $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^nf(i)$, preserves all comparisons and equality strata. The value space and the prescription for $w_H$ do not depend on this auxiliary $D$.

proof.text: Use the coherent-prescription theorem to obtain one simultaneous ν with charts at every singular point, equality with every chart word, and bottom exactly at regular points. This is an existential elimination inside a proof, not a data definition choosing an arbitrary witness.

For every chart C, its final marked ideal has maximal order by C.maximalStages. Apply the fixed engine normalized field to C.history, C.admissible and its final cosupport point. This supplies the leading rational one independently of the coherent-prescription lemma.

Apply the finite-local-upper-bound theorem to the prescribed family at H, using exactly the chart availability, chart-word equality and regularity clauses from the first step. This proves finite image.

For any threshold v and any x outside its upper level, choose the open neighborhood U on which ν H y ≤ ν H x. If v ≤ ν H y held for a y in U, transitivity would give v ≤ ν H x, a contradiction. Therefore the complement is open; the upper level is closed.

The integer_operators theorem preserves and reflects strict order under any iterated integer summation. Expand the lexicographic head order to obtain sumHead D a < sumHead D b iff a < b. Strict monotonicity implies injectivity, hence equality reflection. Expanding the lexicographic head/tail order and checking both bottom cases gives the full-word ≤ equivalence. Express equality as the conjunction of the two inequalities. These arguments work for every D and all words, so in particular for the dimension bounds and the prescribed values in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem normalized_resolution_word_gluing (R : MarkedIdeal.NumericalResolution.{u}) : ∃ ν : ValueFamily.{u} HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord, ∀ {A : EmbeddedResolutionPair.{u}} {n : ℕ} (H : EmbeddedResolutionHistory A n), Admissible ν H → (∀ x : H.X, ¬ IsRegularLocalRing (H.X.presheaf.stalk x) → Nonempty (ResolutionWordChart R H x)) ∧ (∀ (x : H.X) (C : ResolutionWordChart R H x), (R.value C.history ⟨C.supportPoint, C.cosupport⟩).head? = some (MarkedIdeal.rational 1) ∧ ν H x = C.word) ∧ (Set.range (ν H)).Finite ∧ (∀ v : HilbertSamuel.ResolutionWord, IsClosed {x : H.X | v ≤ ν H x}) ∧ (∀ x : H.X, ν H x = ⊥ ↔ IsRegularLocalRing (H.X.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ ∀ (D : ℕ) (_hD : topologicalKrullDim H.X ≤ (D : WithBot ℕ∞)) (x y : H.X), (HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν H x) ≤ HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν H y) ↔ ν H x ≤ ν H y) ∧ (HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν H x) = HilbertSamuel.sumResolutionWord D (ν H y) ↔ ν H x = ν H y)
